[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/6: [source_identity] "For this truth, then" vs "διὰ ταύτην οὖν τὴν ἀλήθειαν": "truth" is wrong; διὰ ταύτην τὴν αἰτίαν/αἰτίαν expected, "for this reason/cause"; [scripture] "Psalm 102 [103]" vs "172 Ps 102 arg.": Wrong bracketed number; should be [101] not [103] for Hebrew numbering; [agency] "the judicial righteousness are glorified" vs "δικαιοσύνη ἡ κριτικὴ δοξάζεται": Singular verb with singular subject; "are" should be "is"; [completeness] "and there is the removal of corruption" vs "φθορᾶς τε ἀφαίρεσις": Missing "τε"/"both" coordination; breaks parallel structure with preceding clause; [completeness] "and the grace kept for successors" vs "καὶ ἡ εἰς διαδόχους φυλασσομένη χάρις": Missing "καὶ"/"and" at start of clause; breaks threefold coordination | part 2/6: [scripture] "Psalm 102 [103]" vs "Ps 103,3a ... Ps 103,4a": Source cites Ps 103 (LXX), which is Ps 104 Hebrew/English, not Ps 102/103.; [scripture] "John 5:17" vs "Ὁ πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται, κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι": Source has no explicit John 5:17 citation; this is editorial addition not in Greek.; [scripture] "Exodus 3:14" vs "Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν": Source has no explicit Exodus 3:14 citation; this is editorial addition not in Greek.; [agency] "being roofed from above by waters with a stable and fixed standing" vs "στεγαζόμενος ἄνωθεν ὕδασιν": Greek is active participle 'roofing/protecting from above with waters', not passive 'being roofed'. | part 3/6: [scripture] "Psalm 73 (74):15" vs "ἑβδομηκοστῷ τρίτῳ": LXX Ps 73:15 does not match; citation is Ps 73 (74):15 in Hebrew numbering but LXX Ps 73 is different. The verse quoted is actually LXX Ps 73:15 = MT Ps 74:15, so bracket should be (74) not (73). The English has 73 (74) which reverses the standard LXX-first convention.; [scripture] "Hosea 10:8" vs "Ἐροῦσι τοῖς ὄρεσι Συγκαλύψατε ἡμᾶς": Source gives no attribution; English adds Hosea 10:8 without brackets as editorial addition, but this is actually Luke 23:30/Rev 6:16 quoting Hosea 10:8. The source lacks any citation.; [agency] "the earth gives springs of water that gush up from the beginning" vs "Πηγὰς ὕδατος ἀναβλυστανούσας τῆς ἀρχῆς καὶ ταῦτα θεοῦ δυνάμει ἡ γῆ δίδωσι": Greek has 'gushing from the beginning' (τῆς ἀρχῆς) modifying springs, not 'from the beginning' as temporal origin; 'gush up from the beginning' misrepresents the syntax where ἀρχῆς is source/origin not temporal start.; [modality] "since the abyss beneath it can neither support nor establish it" vs "οὐ δή που τῆς ὑπούσης ἀβύσσου στηρίζειν αὐτὴν δυναμένης οὐδὲ ἑδρασούσης": Greek has participles 'not at all the underlying abyss being able to support... nor establishing' with causal force, but 'since... can' changes to finite verb construction altering the grammatical texture; however this is borderline. More seriously: 'can neither support nor establish' makes two coordinated abilities, but Greek has δυναμένης only with στηρίζειν, not with ἑδρασούσης which is a participle without δυναμένης. | part 4/6: [agency] "God is said to mock him" vs "Καταπαίζειν δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγεται ὁ θεὸς": Subject is reversed: 'God is said to mock him' should be 'to mock him God is said' or 'he is said to be mocked by God'; but more seriously, αὐτοῦ is genitive 'of him' not accusative 'him'—the syntax is 'to-mock of-him God is said', i.e. 'God is said to mock him' is acceptable. Actually checking again: λέγεται ὁ θεὸς = 'God is said', καταπαίζειν αὐτοῦ = 'to mock him' (genitive of object with compound verb). This is acceptable.; [completeness] "because of its futility" vs "διὰ τὸ μάταιον": τὸ μάταιον is neuter 'the futile thing/vain thing', not 'its futility'—but this is near-synonym. Not reporting.; [agency] "because of how easily it is caught" vs "διὰ τὸ εὐάλωτον": εὐάλωτον means 'easily caught/taken' applied to the opponent, but 'it' refers to 'the futile thing' or the opposition itself; acceptable.; [scripture] "Jeremiah 8:7" vs "Ἱερεμίου": Source has no chapter/verse reference; the English adds (Jeremiah 8:7). This is bracketed editorial note per instructions—do not report.; [scripture] "Exodus 10:2" vs "Ὅσα ἐμπέπαιχα τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις": Source has no Exodus 10:2 reference; English adds it. Bracketed editorial note—do not report.; [completeness] "Others have taken the preceding words about the food supplied to living creatures" vs "Ἄλλοι δὲ περὶ τῆς χορηγουμένης τοῖς ζῴοις τροφῆς ἐξειλήφασι τὰ προκείμενα": τὰ προκείμενα = 'the preceding things/words' is present; 'living creatures' for ζῴοις is fine. No defect.; [agency] "he would be saying that the drawing up of the waters from the sea is his work" vs "ἔργον δὲ τὴν ἐκ θαλάσσης ἀναγωγὴν τῶν ὑδάτων ἂν λέγοι": ἂν λέγοι = 'he would say', but subject is unstated; English supplies 'he' referring back to the author/speaker, but contextually refers to the one speaking about the Son's work. The 'his work' at end is slightly ambiguous—does 'his' refer to Son or the speaker? In context, 'his work' = the Son's work. Greek has ἔργον without possessive. English adds 'his' which is interpretive but clear from context. Not a major error. | part 5/6: [agency] "Others have taken the preceding words" vs "ταύτης γὰρ παρούσης": No 'others' in source; subject is food/nourishment implied from context; [completeness] "about the food supplied to living creatures" vs "ταύτης γὰρ παρούσης": Invented clause; source simply says 'this being present'; [scripture] "Romans 8:11" vs "Ζωοποιήσει τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος πνεύματος ἐν ὑμῖν": Source quotes verbatim but gives no scripture reference; 'Romans 8:11' is editorial addition; [completeness] "and the fear reveals the subjection" vs "τὴν δ' ὑπόταξιν ὁ φόβος μηνύει": Missing 'but/δέ' contrast with preceding clause about glory | part 6/6: [agency] "the sea was subjected by being afraid" vs "θάλασσαν ὑποταχθῆναι φοβηθῆναι": Greek has infinitives 'to be subjected, to be feared' with 'says the psalm'; English adds 'by' making fear the means of subjection, but Greek likely means two parallel things the psalm says (sea subjected, sea feared/feared thing subjected).; [completeness] "the subjection of the earth is the trembling" vs "γῆς ὑπόταξις ὁ τρόμος": English adds 'is' making equation, but Greek is asyndetic: 'of-earth subjection, the trembling...'—could be 'and the subjection of earth [is] the trembling' or 'the earth's subjection [and] the trembling'; the 'is' interpretively smooths syntax.; [source_identity] "Mount Sinai" vs "Σινᾶ": Greek has 'the Sinai mountain' (τοῦ Σινᾶ ὄρους), English inverts to 'Mount Sinai'—minor but changes word order emphasis.
